On real-world industrial data, each predictor already improves feasibility, but the stacked embedding consistently achieves the lowest objective degradation: it (i)~satisfies the operational rules on unseen instances with smaller degradation than any single-model variant, (ii)~picks the most appropriate predictor per decision without prior knowledge of the rule's nature, and (iii)~reduces daily manual adjustment effort while remaining tractable for daily use. Beyond this application, the framework enables optimization tools that adapt to evolving practice without recurrent manual remodeling.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to learn implicit feasibility constraints for log-truck routing and scheduling, embedding predictors into a MILP to reduce manual adjustments.
motivation: Real-world routing problems have evolving operational rules that are hard to update in optimization tools, leading to manual plan adjustments.
method: Trains a GNN, decision tree, and linear regression on historical data, then embeds each as linearized constraints in a MILP, with a stacking mechanism to select the best predictor per decision.
result: The stacked embedding achieves the lowest objective degradation while satisfying operational rules on unseen instances, reducing manual adjustment effort.
conclusion: The framework enables optimization tools to adapt to evolving rules without manual remodeling, with potential applications beyond log transportation.

title: Bayesian Equilibria Of Heterogeneous Non-Atomic Routing Games With Private Information
authors: Alexia Ambrogio, Leonardo Cianfanelli, Giacomo Como, Paolo Frasca
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-atomic Bayesian routing games whereby a transportation network is shared by two types of traffic: a coordinated fleet and a mass of selfish users. The links in the network are characterized by travel time functions that depend both on the aggregate flow on the link and on a random state of the world [MATH] that, in general, is not directly observable. Rather, we assume that both the fleet coordinator and the selfish users know the prior distribution of [MATH], observe (different) private messages that are correlated with [MATH] and possibly among themselves, and make routing decisions based on such heterogeneous partial information. Under the assumption that both the state of the world and the private message sets are finite, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a Bayesian equilibrium for the ensuing Bayesian routing game.
tldr: This paper studies Bayesian equilibria in non-atomic routing games with heterogeneous private information, focusing on transportation networks with coordinated and selfish users.
motivation: To understand how partial and heterogeneous information affects routing decisions and equilibrium existence in transportation networks.
method: The authors model the problem as a Bayesian routing game with finite state and message spaces, and prove existence and uniqueness of Bayesian equilibrium using fixed-point arguments.
result: Existence and uniqueness of a Bayesian equilibrium are established under the assumption of finite state and message sets.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for analyzing routing games with private information, but its direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics is not evident.

title: The Complex Spectral Flow: Spectral Conditions For Two-Parameter Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the -- a virtual [MATH]-representation assembling the eigenvalue winding numbers of the linearization at an isolated two-parameter critical point for [MATH] bifurcation problems -- and prove that, for maximal twisted orbit types, the coefficient of the local bifurcation invariant in [MATH] reduces to a closed-form dimension formula, bypassing the standard pipeline of basic degree factorization and Burnside ring multiplication entirely. When the eigenvalue dependence is holomorphic, topological cancellation among winding numbers is impossible, yielding unconditional local and global bifurcation guarantees. As applications, we establish the macroscopic escape of symmetric Hopf branches in [MATH]-equivariant systems and of patterned relative equilibria for the complex Ginzburg--Landau equation directly from spectral data.
tldr: This paper introduces a virtual representation for eigenvalue winding numbers in two-parameter equivariant bifurcation problems, providing a closed-form dimension formula for bifurcation invariants.
motivation: To simplify the computation of local bifurcation invariants in two-parameter equivariant systems, bypassing the standard pipeline of basic degree factorization and Burnside ring multiplication.
method: The authors define a virtual representation that assembles eigenvalue winding numbers and prove that for maximal twisted orbit types, the coefficient of the local bifurcation invariant reduces to a closed-form dimension formula.
result: Topological cancellation among winding numbers is impossible when eigenvalue dependence is holomorphic, yielding unconditional bifurcation guarantees. Applications include symmetric Hopf branches and patterned relative equilibria for the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation.
conclusion: The work provides a spectral approach to bifurcation analysis that simplifies computations and offers unconditional guarantees for holomorphic dependencies, with potential applications in equivariant dynamical systems.

title: Sequence Reconstruction For Substitution Channel: New Sufficient Conditions And Algorithms
authors: Chen Wang, Eitan Yaakobi, Yiwei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the sequence reconstruction problem, a codeword [MATH] is transmitted through several identical channels where each channel produces a noisy read of [MATH], and the problem is to analyze how to uniquely reconstruct [MATH] based on these noisy reads. Levenshtein has studied the minimum number of reads which guarantees unique reconstruction of [MATH], which is one sufficient condition for unique reconstruction. In this paper, we move on to a different perspective and propose a new framework for unique reconstruction. Our new sufficient condition for unique reconstruction takes both the number of reads and the distances among the reads into consideration. We offer both theoretical analysis and corresponding efficient reconstruction algorithms for our reconstruction framework.
tldr: This paper studies sequence reconstruction from noisy reads over substitution channels, proposing new sufficient conditions and algorithms for unique reconstruction.
motivation: To improve upon Levenshtein's sufficient condition for unique reconstruction by considering both the number of reads and their distances.
method: The authors propose a new framework that incorporates distances among reads, and develop efficient reconstruction algorithms based on this framework.
result: New sufficient conditions for unique reconstruction are derived, and corresponding algorithms are provided with theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The work offers a more flexible approach to sequence reconstruction, with potential applications in DNA storage and communication.

title: A Two-Channel F-Transform Representation For Early Trajectory Characterization In Iterated Correlation Dynamics
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonlinear iterative procedures generate high-dimensional trajectories whose early behavior is informative but difficult to compare directly. This paper studies a soft-computing representation problem: how to convert a short early trajectory segment into compact, interpretable, fixed-dimensional fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry. The problem is investigated for iterated Pearson correlation matrices, a nonlinear matrix iteration historically connected with CONCOR-type blockmodeling and repeated-correlation methods. The proposed descriptor uses two logarithmic signals from the early post-transient regime: a step-size signal, measuring contraction magnitude, and a contraction-ratio signal, measuring local contraction evolution. Each signal is projected onto a three-node triangular fuzzy partition using zero-degree F-transform coefficients and one centered first-degree coefficient. This yields an eight-dimensional two-channel representation separating local level from local trend and contraction magnitude from contraction evolution. Across 22 matrix dimensions with 1000 trajectories per dimension, the descriptor is compared with raw trajectory samples, statistical summaries, and PCA-compressed raw features using Random Forest regression for convergence-length approximation. It achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), while improving over the step-size-only F-transform descriptor (0.5001). Repeated random-split and shifted-window experiments confirm stability. PCA and clustering further show reproducible low-dimensional organization, with the first two principal components explaining 84.26% of variance and k = 3 favored by the mean silhouette criterion.
tldr: This paper proposes a fuzzy-transform-based descriptor for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, achieving compact representation with competitive convergence prediction accuracy.
motivation: To convert short early trajectory segments from nonlinear iterative procedures into compact, interpretable fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry.
method: Two logarithmic signals (step-size and contraction-ratio) from the early post-transient regime are projected onto triangular fuzzy partitions using zero-degree and first-degree F-transform coefficients, forming an eight-dimensional two-channel representation. Random Forest regression is used for convergence-length approximation.
result: The descriptor achieves mean R^2 = 0.6480, close to raw trajectories (0.6518) and statistical summaries (0.6528), and improves over step-size-only F-transform (0.5001). PCA shows 84.26% variance explained by first two components, and clustering favors k=3.
conclusion: The proposed representation is effective for early trajectory characterization in iterated correlation dynamics, with potential applications in soft computing and data analysis, but no direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: Optimal Experimental Design For Passive Imaging Source Problems
authors: Christian Aarset, Thorsten Hohage, Georg Stadler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work focuses on optimal experimental design (OED) methods for passive imaging. We adopt a Bayesian inverse problem framework for passive imaging source problems, primarily focusing on spatially uncorrelated sources and systems governed by the Helmholtz equation. A major challenge in passive imaging is that the use of correlation data causes the observation dimension to grow quadratically with the number of sensor locations, compounding the computational difficulty of finding optimal designs. To overcome the computational bottleneck of repeated PDE solves in optimal design algorithms, we develop a two-level, low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective. This effectively decouples the problem into an offline and an online phase, enabling efficient evaluation of the design objective and its gradient without additional PDE solves. Our numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm efficiently scales to large problems and that the resulting optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
tldr: This paper develops optimal experimental design methods for passive imaging source problems using Bayesian inverse problems and low-rank approximations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Passive imaging source problems suffer from high computational cost due to quadratic growth of correlation data with sensor count; efficient design algorithms are needed.
method: A two-level, low-rank approximation of the A-optimal design objective is developed, decoupling the problem into offline and online phases to avoid repeated PDE solves.
result: The algorithm scales efficiently to large problems and optimal designs significantly outperform random sensor placements in minimizing posterior uncertainty.
conclusion: The proposed method enables practical OED for passive imaging, but the work is entirely classical and unrelated to quantum systems or information thermodynamics.

title: Robust Repair Of Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Wilton Kim, Stanislav Kruglik, Gaojun Luo, Han Mao Kiah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of robust repair of a single erasure in Reed--Solomon codes under low communication bandwidth. Focusing on the Guruswami--Wootters trace repair framework, we investigate whether a failed node can be correctly repaired in the presence of erroneous responses from helper nodes. Equivalently, we view the collection of downloaded traces as a code, which we call the repair-trace code. By characterizing the zero coefficients of the associated polynomial in terms of cyclotomic cosets, we derive upper bounds on the dimension [MATH] that allow correction of a given number of erroneous traces [MATH], as well as lower bounds on the minimum distance as a function of [MATH]. For the case [MATH], we exploit explicit formulas for cyclotomic coset representatives to obtain the exact optimal dimension bound for single-error correction. We also propose two efficient robust repair schemes. Our first scheme achieves the error-correction capability guaranteed by the BCH bound. To approach a stronger bound based on character sums, we develop a second scheme that tolerates more errors at the cost of an additional factor [MATH] in computational complexity.
tldr: This paper studies robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes under erroneous helper responses, focusing on the Guruswami-Wootters trace repair framework.
motivation: To ensure correct repair of a failed node in distributed storage systems even when some helper nodes provide erroneous responses.
method: Characterizes zero coefficients of associated polynomials via cyclotomic cosets to derive bounds on repair-trace code dimension and minimum distance; proposes two efficient robust repair schemes.
result: Derives upper and lower bounds on dimension for error correction, obtains exact optimal dimension for single-error correction, and proposes schemes achieving BCH bound and a stronger character-sum bound.
conclusion: Provides theoretical bounds and practical schemes for robust repair of Reed-Solomon codes, with trade-offs between error tolerance and computational complexity.

title: Multi-parameter Persistence In Dynamical Systems For Maximizing Effects Of Control Inputs
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new topological method to naturally extend a partial function [MATH] on a ``generalization'' of a metric space [MATH] equipped with a dynamical system [MATH], to a function [MATH] with parameters [MATH], which allows us to apply existing topological data analysis techniques to functions defined on the whole space. Moreover, given a function [MATH] that evaluates the ``quality'' of points within [MATH], using this extended function, one can construct a sufficient condition for the existence of an optimal [MATH]-perturbation path from any point into [MATH] that minimizes the value of [MATH] under the condition [MATH]. In addition, if the domain [MATH] is finite, then the function [MATH] can be computed recursively. As an application, for a given partial evaluation function on a space equipped with a dynamical system, one can construct a three-parameter filtration associated with its extension, which naturally identifies minimal paths. This clarifies the relationship among three factors: the evaluation of the cost norm, the strength of control, and the resulting value.
tldr: This paper introduces a topological method to extend partial functions on dynamical systems for optimizing control inputs, with applications to path planning.
motivation: To develop a framework that uses topological data analysis to find optimal perturbation paths in dynamical systems under cost constraints.
method: The authors extend partial functions on metric spaces with dynamical systems to full functions with parameters, enabling the application of persistent homology. They construct a three-parameter filtration to identify minimal paths.
result: A sufficient condition for the existence of optimal perturbation paths is derived, and a recursive computation is possible for finite domains.
conclusion: The method clarifies the trade-off between cost norm, control strength, and resulting value, offering a new tool for control optimization in dynamical systems.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization For Rotatable Antenna-Enabled Uplink Noma Systems
authors: Yixuan Li, Jun Wang, Hongbo Xu, Ji Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a rotatable antenna (RA)-enabled uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system, where a base station equipped with multiple independently RAs serves both ground and aerial users. Specifically, we formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, user power allocation, and RA rotation. To make the problem tractable, a new block coordinate descent-based algorithm is developed, in which the receive beamforming is updated via the minimum mean square error criterion, while the power allocation and RA rotation are handled by fractional programming and successive convex approximation. Numerical results demonstrate the EE superiority of the proposed RA-NOMA scheme over several benchmarks.
tldr: This paper optimizes energy efficiency in a rotatable antenna-enabled uplink NOMA system using joint beamforming, power allocation, and antenna rotation.
motivation: To improve energy efficiency in wireless communication systems with rotatable antennas and NOMA, addressing the need for higher spectral and energy efficiency in future networks.
method: A block coordinate descent algorithm is developed, updating receive beamforming via MMSE, and handling power allocation and RA rotation via fractional programming and successive convex approximation.
result: The proposed RA-NOMA scheme achieves superior energy efficiency compared to several benchmarks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of combining rotatable antennas with NOMA for energy-efficient uplink communications, with implications for future wireless system design.

title: Asymmetry Of Entropy Invariants For Generic Mixing $Z^n$-Actions
authors: Valery V. Ryzhikov Mikhail V. Engelgardt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that for a mixing [MATH]-action, [MATH], there exists a Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy that is zero for this action and completely positive for its inverse. We prove that this property is generic for the mixing [MATH]-actions.
tldr: The paper proves that for generic mixing Z^n-actions, the Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy can be zero for the action and completely positive for its inverse, demonstrating asymmetry of entropy invariants.
motivation: To understand the asymmetry of entropy invariants under inversion for mixing Z^n-actions, which is a fundamental question in ergodic theory.
method: The authors use generic properties of mixing actions and entropy theory, likely employing Baire category arguments and constructions of mixing actions with prescribed entropy behavior.
result: It is shown that for a generic mixing Z^n-action, there exists a Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy that is zero for the action and completely positive for its inverse.
conclusion: This result highlights a generic asymmetry in entropy invariants, which may have implications for the classification of mixing actions and the understanding of entropy in dynamical systems.

title: A Low-rank Interpolatory Projection Algorithm For Solving Large-scale T-Sylvester Equations
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers large-scale T-Sylvester equations of the form [MATH], which admit a low-rank solution. It is shown that when the unique solution of the T-Sylvester equation is low-rank, the problem naturally reduces to a tangential interpolation problem via oblique projection. The specific interpolation points and tangential directions needed to obtain the low-rank solution are not known a priori, thus requiring an iterative approach. An iterative interpolatory projection algorithm is proposed based on these interpolation conditions, which iteratively refines the interpolation data as the projection matrices expand in the number of columns. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges with projection matrices having significantly fewer columns compared to existing Krylov-subspace-based projection methods, confirming the superiority of the proposed algorithm over existing approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative interpolatory projection algorithm for solving large-scale T-Sylvester equations with low-rank solutions.
motivation: T-Sylvester equations arise in various applications, and existing Krylov-subspace methods require large projection spaces; the goal is to develop a more efficient algorithm.
method: The problem is reduced to a tangential interpolation problem via oblique projection, and an iterative algorithm refines interpolation data as projection matrices expand.
result: Numerical examples show the proposed algorithm converges with significantly fewer columns than existing Krylov-subspace methods.
conclusion: The algorithm offers a superior approach for low-rank T-Sylvester equations, with potential for further optimization and application to other matrix equations.

title: Iterative Thresholding Pursuit With Continuation For $\ell_{1-2}$-Regularized Sparse Recovery
authors: Junxi Wu, Zeyu Dong, Jun-Feng Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse recovery aims to reconstruct sparse signals from underdetermined and possibly noisy linear measurements. Existing [MATH] iterative thresholding schemes are first-order methods. We propose an iterative thresholding pursuit method with continuation (ITP-C) for [MATH]-regularized sparse recovery. The method goes beyond first-order thresholding by combining the active-set identification capability of the [MATH] proximal step with a restricted least-squares pursuit step that provides a second-order update on the identified support. The support is generated adaptively by the thresholding update, and no prior knowledge of the true sparsity level is required. To control the possible instability of the pursuit step while preserving the descent structure of the continuation scheme, we impose a strict descent check with respect to the dynamic objective. We establish convergence of the generated sequence under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz framework and prove a local oracle-type property after correct support identification. Numerical experiments on synthetic sparse recovery and image reconstruction illustrate the descent preservation of the proposed safeguard and demonstrate the improved recovery performance of ITP-C over the state-of-the-art baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative thresholding pursuit method with continuation for ℓ1-2 regularized sparse recovery, improving reconstruction performance over existing methods.
motivation: To overcome limitations of first-order iterative thresholding methods for sparse recovery by incorporating second-order updates and adaptive support identification.
method: Combines a proximal step for active-set identification with a restricted least-squares pursuit step, controlled by a strict descent check and continuation scheme.
result: The method achieves better recovery performance on synthetic and image reconstruction tasks compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with convergence guarantees under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz framework.
conclusion: The proposed ITP-C method offers a robust and efficient approach for ℓ1-2 regularized sparse recovery, with potential applications in signal and image processing.

title: Trace-Class Results For Mcmc Algorithms For Student-t Regression Models
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider MCMC algorithms for Student-[MATH] regression models. We investigate the efficiency of Markov chains based on the algorithms in terms of whether trace-class results hold or not. We first consider the case where the regression coefficients and error variance follow the invariant improper prior distributions. The Markov operator associated with a standard data augmentation algorithm is not trace-class but that associated with a collpased Gibbs algorithm is trace-class. We next consider the case where the parameters follow a normal-inverse gamma distribution. In this case, the standard Markov operator is trace-class.
tldr: This paper analyzes trace-class properties of MCMC algorithms for Student-t regression models, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of Markov chains in Bayesian regression with heavy-tailed errors.
method: Theoretical analysis of trace-class property for standard data augmentation and collapsed Gibbs algorithms under different prior distributions.
result: The collapsed Gibbs algorithm is trace-class under improper priors, while the standard algorithm is not; under normal-inverse gamma priors, the standard algorithm is trace-class.
conclusion: The findings guide algorithm choice for efficient MCMC in Student-t regression, but have no connection to quantum systems.

title: Sparse Recovery Via $\ell_1^2-\eta\ell_2^2$ Minimization
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The weighted difference of squared norms (WDSN) penalty [MATH] with [MATH] has attracted considerable attention due to its strong sparsity-promoting ability and favorable reconstruction performance in compressed sensing and inverse problems. However, exact recovery guarantees and restricted isometry property (RIP) analysis for WDSN minimization have not yet been established. In this paper, we address this gap. First, we establish sufficient conditions for the exact recovery of [MATH]-sparse signals based on the null space property (NSP). Then, under the [MATH]-RIP condition, we derive stable recovery guarantees for both [MATH]-sparse signals and general signals, and characterize upper bounds on the reconstruction error. Furthermore, we propose a WDSN-based regularized model to handle both noiseless and noisy observations in a unified framework. To design an efficient algorithm, we derive an explicit formula for the proximal operator of the WDSN functional. Based on this proximal solver, we develop a suitable variable-splitting scheme within the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and establish its global convergence under some mild conditions. Finally, numerical experiments show that the proposed method outperforms the iterative half variation method in both noiseless and noisy sparse recovery tasks.
tldr: This paper establishes exact recovery guarantees and RIP analysis for WDSN minimization in compressed sensing, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To fill the gap in theoretical guarantees for WDSN minimization, which is known for strong sparsity promotion but lacked rigorous recovery conditions.
method: Derives null space property and RIP-based sufficient conditions for exact and stable recovery, proposes a regularized model, and develops an ADMM algorithm with proximal operator.
result: Provides first exact recovery guarantees for WDSN minimization and demonstrates superior performance over iterative half variation in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work advances compressed sensing theory but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid systems.

title: Bv Construction Of Susy Vertex Algebras From Susy Factorization Algebras
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct [MATH] supersymmetric (SUSY) vertex algebras from supersymmetric enhancements of Costello--Gwilliam factorization algebras on super Riemann surfaces. Introducing SUSY factorization algebras defined on embedded SUSY disks together with natural symmetry conditions, we prove a SUSY analogue of the Costello--Gwilliam extraction theorem. As an application, we study the holomorphic sigma model in the BV formalism. For a linear target, we obtain the free [MATH]-[MATH] system and recover its structure as a SUSY vertex algebra. For general complex targets, we describe the descent of the theory under coordinate changes and identify the resulting SUSY vertex algebra with the chiral de Rham complex. We further show that Ricci-flat K\"ahler and hyperk\"ahler targets give rise to [MATH] and [MATH] supersymmetric enhancements introduced by Ben-Zvi--Heluani--Szczesny.
tldr: This paper constructs supersymmetric vertex algebras from supersymmetric enhancements of factorization algebras on super Riemann surfaces, with applications to holomorphic sigma models and the chiral de Rham complex.
motivation: To develop a rigorous mathematical framework for supersymmetric vertex algebras using factorization algebras, extending Costello–Gwilliam's work to the supersymmetric setting.
method: Introduces SUSY factorization algebras on embedded SUSY disks with symmetry conditions, proves a SUSY analogue of the Costello–Gwilliam extraction theorem, and applies the formalism to holomorphic sigma models in the BV formalism.
result: For linear targets, obtains the free β-γ system; for general complex targets, identifies the resulting SUSY vertex algebra with the chiral de Rham complex; shows Ricci-flat Kähler and hyperkähler targets yield N=1 and N=2 supersymmetric enhancements.
conclusion: Provides a unified construction of SUSY vertex algebras from geometric data, with implications for supersymmetric field theories and string theory.

title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers For Generalized Newtonian Models
authors: Stefano Zampini, Daniele Boffi, Gurt Dovletov, Peter Markowich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic [MATH]-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the [MATH]-Laplacian and [MATH]-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for [MATH], [MATH], with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.
tldr: This paper introduces an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for solving generalized Newtonian models, focusing on numerical methods for nonlinear PDEs.
motivation: To develop efficient and robust numerical solvers for generalized Newtonian fluid models that are computationally challenging due to nonlinear constitutive relations.
method: The authors replace the nonlinear gradient dependence with an auxiliary scalar variable representing squared magnitude, leading to a sequence of linear elliptic problems. They construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space, prove convexity and convergence, and propose practical time discretizations including operator-splitting and adaptive pseudo-transient methods.
result: The method yields exponential convergence for the minimizing-movement scheme, rigorous convergence for p-Laplacian and p-Stokes models with p in (1,∞), and numerical experiments show robustness and mesh-independent iteration counts.
conclusion: The auxiliary gradient-flow framework provides a viable alternative to Newton's method for generalized Newtonian models, with potential extensions to other variational problems.

title: Direct Reconstruction For Acoustic Inverse Born Scattering
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation in two dimensions, i.e., the task to recover a compactly supported penetrable two-dimensional scatterer from full knowledge of the associated far field data or, equivalently, the far field operator. Although this problem is uniquely solvable, it is severely ill-posed and nonlinear. In the regime of weak scattering, the Born approximation yields a linearized relation between the contrast and the far field data, thus overcoming the second difficulty. This linear setting allows to build on recent work on linearized electrical impedance tomography, which relies on triangular Zernike decompositions, to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that expresses the expansion coefficients of the contrast in terms of those of the far field data. By choosing the expansion functions appropriately, the resulting system matrix decouples into separate (infinite) triangular systems for the spatial angular frequencies in the contrast. Consequently, each of these systems can be solved independently by performing forward substitutions. Our numerical experiments indicate that this approach, combined with an adequate regularization method, remains effective even when applied to full nonlinear far field data beyond the Born regime.
tldr: This paper presents a direct reconstruction method for the acoustic inverse Born scattering problem using triangular Zernike decompositions.
motivation: To overcome the nonlinearity and ill-posedness of the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation.
method: The Born approximation linearizes the problem, then triangular Zernike expansions decouple the system into independent triangular systems solved by forward substitution.
result: Numerical experiments show the method remains effective even beyond the Born regime with appropriate regularization.
conclusion: The approach provides an explicit reconstruction formula and may be extended to other inverse problems.

title: Search-Time Contamination In Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation In Public Benchmark Evaluation
authors: Yongjie Wang, Xinyue Zhang, Kunhong Yao, Zhiwei Zeng, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Zhiqi Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmarks enable fair and reproducible evaluation of LLM reasoning, but they become fragile for deep research agents that actively search the web during inference. Such agents may retrieve public benchmark metadata, question context, or even ground-truth answers via web search. This gives rise to Search-Time Contamination (STC), where external retrieval bypasses intended reasoning and inflates measured performance. We systematically study STC in deep research agent evaluation. We define three contamination types with increasing severity, namely Benchmark Metadata Leakage, Question-Context Leakage, and Explicit Answer Leakage, and develop detection algorithms to identify them and quantify their impact on agent performance. Evaluating modern deep research agents on six public benchmarks, we find that STC is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4%. Our findings show that existing evaluations may overestimate true reasoning ability. We therefore advocate contamination-aware practices, including isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.
tldr: This paper studies how deep research agents can inflate benchmark scores by retrieving answers via web search during inference, a phenomenon called Search-Time Contamination.
motivation: Public benchmarks are used to evaluate LLM reasoning, but deep research agents that search the web during inference may inadvertently access benchmark data, leading to overestimated performance.
method: The authors define three types of contamination (metadata leakage, question-context leakage, explicit answer leakage) and develop detection algorithms to identify and quantify contamination in six public benchmarks.
result: Search-Time Contamination is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4% in modern deep research agents.
conclusion: The findings advocate for contamination-aware evaluation practices such as isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.

title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning And Algorithmic Collusion
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical learning arguments suggest an affirmative answer: ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency. In contrast, recent work on algorithmic collusion suggests that strategic obliviousness -- deliberately ignoring competitor prices -- may facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this modeling choice in a stylized competitive market with unknown noisy demand, in which multiple sellers repeatedly set prices and estimate demand via iterated least squares, and either incorporate competitors' prices into their demand models (informed) or ignore them (oblivious). We first show that, relative to a monopolist, an oblivious seller in a competitive market must explore more aggressively to compensate for the loss of dynamic competitor information. Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.
tldr: This paper studies whether pricing algorithms should model competitors' prices, finding that incorporating competitor information leads to competitive outcomes and higher profits, while obliviousness can cause transient collusive patterns but not sustained collusion.
motivation: To resolve the tension between classical learning arguments favoring inclusion of competitor prices and recent work suggesting obliviousness may facilitate collusion.
method: The authors model a competitive market with multiple sellers using iterated least squares to estimate demand, comparing oblivious sellers (ignore competitor prices) with informed sellers (include them), and analyze market dynamics and Nash equilibria.
result: Oblivious sellers must explore more aggressively; all-oblivious markets converge to competitive outcomes under sufficient exploration but exhibit pseudo-equilibria when exploration decays; informed sellers outperform oblivious ones; the unique Nash equilibrium is the all-informed market.
conclusion: Incorporating competitor information with sufficient price exploration is a reliable strategy; collusive patterns from obliviousness are transient and not robust.

title: Willing But Unable: Separating Refusal From Capability In Code LLMs Via Abliteration
authors: Cristina Carleo, Pietro Liguori, Naghmeh Ivaki, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing a labeled vulnerable code at scale is a recurring obstacle for learning-based vulnerability detection: mined corpora carry substantial label noise, and existing LLM-based augmentation propagates these inaccuracies because it transforms vulnerable seeds rather than synthesising vulnerabilities from a specification. A complementary route is to start from safe code and ask an instruction-tuned LLM to inject a specified CWE (which would shift the labeling burden from open-ended detection to bounded binary confirmation) but safety-aligned code LLMs systematically refuse such prompts. This paper is a preliminary feasibility study of abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that orthogonally projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, as a tool to remove this barrier. We use Python and CWE-89 (SQL injection) as a case study, evaluating the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family at 3B, 7B, and 14B parameters on safe samples drawn from PromSec and SafeCoder, replicated three times per condition. We find that (i) refusal on injection prompts is strongly size- and prompt-context-dependent: the 14B refuses 100% of prompts, the 7B refuses 73% of PromSec but only 5% of SafeCoder, whereas the 3B is essentially never blocked; (ii) abliteration reduces refusal to zero or near-zero across all sizes while leaving syntactic validity above 93%, supporting the view that, in this setting, refusal can be detached from measured code-generation capability; and (iii) the post-abliteration injection rate remains capacity-bound (88-97% on the 14B, 89-90% on the 7B, and 25-48% on the 3B) separating willingness, which abliteration unlocks, from capability, which scales with parameters. Vulnerability verdicts are produced by a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) followed by manual adjudication by two authors on detector-positive outputs.
tldr: This paper explores abliteration, a weight-editing technique to bypass safety alignment in code LLMs for vulnerability injection, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To enable instruction-tuned code LLMs to inject specific vulnerabilities (CWEs) into safe code for generating labeled vulnerable datasets, overcoming refusal due to safety alignment.
method: Applied abliteration (low-rank weight edit projecting out the refusal direction) to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) and evaluated on Python code with CWE-89 (SQL injection) using PromSec and SafeCoder datasets.
result: Abliteration reduced refusal to near-zero while maintaining syntactic validity >93%; injection success was capacity-bound (88-97% for 14B, 25-48% for 3B).
conclusion: Refusal can be separated from code-generation capability via abliteration, enabling scalable generation of labeled vulnerable code, but the approach is limited to specific CWEs and models.

title: Rh+: Row-Hit-Optimized Scheduling For PIM-based Llm Inference
authors: Yongchan Jung, Shafayat Mowla Anik, Byeong Kil Lee, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model inference on processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures promises to break the memory wall by performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations directly within HBM3 DRAM banks. Prior work identifies the power constraint timing parameter nCCDAB as the primary performance bottleneck and optimizes scheduling accordingly. We demonstrate that for GEMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding, the DRAM row cycle time (nRC) is 10 to 11 times larger than nCCDAB. Consequently, nCCDAB is entirely masked, rendering prior nCCDAB-focused optimizations ineffective for these workloads. The root cause is inherited host-centric address interleaving, which forces every all-bank MAC command into a different DRAM row. We propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row. Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows that RH+ delivers 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
tldr: This paper proposes RH+ scheduling to optimize PIM-based LLM inference by addressing DRAM row cycle time bottlenecks.
motivation: Prior PIM scheduling optimizations focused on nCCDAB timing, but for GEMV operations in LLM decoding, nRC is the dominant bottleneck due to host-centric address interleaving.
method: The authors identify that nRC is 10-11x larger than nCCDAB, making previous optimizations ineffective. They propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same DRAM row.
result: Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
conclusion: RH+ scheduling effectively mitigates the row cycle time bottleneck for PIM-based LLM inference, offering significant performance and energy gains.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Cyber Risk Analytics And Model Reliability Assessment For Intelligent Governance Of U.s. Critical Infrastructure: An XGBoost And SHAP-Based Intrusion Detection Framework
authors: B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Arifur Rahman, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel, Md. Iqbal Hossan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing penetrations of the critical infrastructure sector in the United States with intelligent digital technologies have greatly increased exposure to advanced cyber adversaries and operational vulnerabilities. AI-powered governance and automated decision-making systems are becoming a key part of the operation of critical infrastructure systems, including energy, healthcare, transportation, financial services, and communication infrastructure, in order to improve efficiency and strategic management. The growing cyber threat environment, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDos) attacks, botnets, ransomware, and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) pose significant challenges to infrastructure resilience, cyber security reliability, and governance trustworthiness. In a changing attack landscape and dynamic network environment, traditional cybersecurity mechanisms can often fall short of meeting the evolving needs and protecting critical systems. This study will develop a resilient cyber risk analytics and model reliability assessment framework to support intelligent governance and decision support for cyber risk exposure in the U.S. critical infrastructure environment. This study is based on the CICIDS2017 dataset for the development and testing of intrusion detection system models and cyber risk prediction models based on machine learning. Various classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree are used to detect malicious activities on the network and determine the level of cyber risk. Furthermore, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques are integrated to enhance transparency, interpretability, and trust in cybersecurity decision-making processes. The proposed framework presents the reliability and resilience of the model by having various performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, and false positive rate.
tldr: This paper applies XGBoost and SHAP for intrusion detection in U.S. critical infrastructure, focusing on cyber risk analytics and model reliability.
motivation: To address the growing cyber threats to critical infrastructure and the limitations of traditional cybersecurity mechanisms.
method: Uses the CICIDS2017 dataset and machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree) with Explainable AI (SHAP) for intrusion detection and risk prediction.
result: The proposed framework demonstrates high performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) and enhanced interpretability via SHAP.
conclusion: The framework supports intelligent governance and decision-making for cyber risk exposure, but further validation on real-world data is needed.

title: An Improved Cnn-lstm Based Intrusion Detection System For IoT Networks
authors: Mohammad Tariq Ikhlas, Pohanyar Khowaja Khil, Malik Muhammad Mueed Aslam, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of IoT devices, security concerns have dramatically escalated and intrusion detection systems have become critical for protecting networked environments. This paper presents an improved CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection model that combines multi-class classification, dataset integration, and temporal feature learning to enhance detection performance in IoT networks. Using network traffic data, the proposed approach is evaluated on intrusion detection tasks and achieves an accuracy of approximately 97%. Experimental results demonstrate that the model effectively detects multiple attack categories while maintaining stable training and validation performance. The integration of convolutional and recurrent neural network components enables the framework to capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of network traffic, improving overall intrusion detection capability in IoT environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection system for IoT networks, achieving 97% accuracy on network traffic data.
motivation: IoT security is critical due to rapid device proliferation, and existing intrusion detection systems need improvement.
method: A hybrid CNN-LSTM model is used to capture spatial and temporal features from network traffic data for multi-class classification.
result: The model achieves approximately 97% accuracy in detecting multiple attack categories with stable training and validation performance.
conclusion: The approach enhances intrusion detection in IoT environments, but further work is needed for real-world deployment and generalization.

title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity For Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis For Sparta Rf And Cyber Threat Detection
authors: van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft require rapid, lightweight, and reliable onboard detection of cyber-RF threats. Using the SPARTA attack model, we analyze the latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models -- Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP -- for detecting uplink jamming, Fake-NR spoofing, payload manipulation, ground-segment compromise, and unauthorized command injection. We present a physics-informed theoretical analysis of each model's computational complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity, and latency scaling, supported by empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms generated via BandErasure, FakeNR, and NoiseBurst corruption modes. Results show that Logistic Regression achieves microsecond-level inference with only a 1\% accuracy drop relative to Random Forest, making it an effective TinyML baseline for onboard autonomy. The study also identifies opportunities for advancing spacecraft cybersecurity through richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures, building on recent progress in edge intelligence and trustworthy AI.
tldr: This paper evaluates TinyML models for cyber-RF threat detection in autonomous spacecraft, focusing on latency-accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft need lightweight onboard detection of cyber-RF threats, but existing solutions may be too heavy or slow.
method: The authors analyze Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP using physics-informed theoretical analysis (complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity) and empirical tests on adversarial RF spectrograms.
result: Logistic Regression achieves microsecond inference with only 1% accuracy drop compared to Random Forest, making it a suitable TinyML baseline.
conclusion: The study suggests future work on richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures for spacecraft cybersecurity.

title: Towards Worst-case Hardness For Low-Noise Lpn
authors: Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, Hai Hoang Nguyen, Kel Zin Tan, Prashant Nalini Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hardness of the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem is a foundational assumption in cryptography, forming the basis of constructions ranging from symmetric-key primitives to public-key encryption and beyond. A central open question is whether the average-case hardness of LPN can be based on worst-case complexity assumptions, as has been achieved for the analogous Learning With Errors (LWE) problem. Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN [BLVW19, YZ21] rely on statistical smoothing of linear codes, which inherently limits the resulting average-case hardness to noise rates as large as [MATH], which is insufficient for public-key applications. We explore a new approach towards obtaining such reductions: rather than requiring that random sparse combinations of the rows of the generator matrix of a code be statistically close to uniform, we only require that they be computationally indistinguishable from uniform. This leads to a clean win-win structure: we show that any efficient LPN solver can be transformed into a pair of efficient algorithms [MATH] such that for every matrix [MATH] of appropriate dimensions over [MATH], either [MATH] decodes the code generated by [MATH] from random noise, or [MATH] distinguishes random noisy codewords of the dual of this code from uniform. By instantiating this reduction with appropriate parameters, we obtain the average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate [MATH] for any constant [MATH], assuming the worst-case simultaneous hardness of decoding a code from random noise and distinguishing random noisy codewords of its dual from uniform. In particular, setting [MATH], our reduction yields LPN hardness in the parameter regime required for Alekhnovich's construction of public-key encryption [Ale03], a regime that was previously inaccessible via worst-case reductions.
tldr: This paper presents a new approach to proving worst-case hardness for the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem, a foundational assumption in cryptography, by relaxing statistical smoothing to computational indistinguishability.
motivation: Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN only work for high noise rates, insufficient for public-key cryptography. The authors aim to achieve reductions for low-noise LPN, which is needed for applications like Alekhnovich's encryption scheme.
method: The authors propose a win-win reduction: any efficient LPN solver yields either a decoder for a linear code or a distinguisher for its dual. They replace statistical smoothing with computational indistinguishability to handle low noise rates.
result: They obtain average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate (1/n^c) for any constant c, assuming worst-case hardness of decoding and distinguishing dual codewords. For c=1, this matches the regime needed for public-key encryption.
conclusion: This work provides a new path to worst-case hardness for low-noise LPN, potentially enabling public-key cryptography based on LPN, but the assumptions are stronger than typical worst-case ones.

title: Exploring Cooperation Mechanisms Via Reinforcement Learning In Network Common-pool Resource Games
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in resource-constrained populations requires allocation mechanisms that balance individual incentives, resource sustainability, and distributional fairness. This paper proposes a network common-pool resource game in which individuals are embedded in complex networks, participate in multiple overlapping local resource pools, and face endogenous resource constraints during strategy evolution. Within this framework, we first examine two representative allocation mechanisms, equal allocation and proportional allocation. The results show that equal allocation produces fair but inefficient outcomes by weakening contribution incentives, whereas proportional allocation can temporarily promote cooperation but amplifies accumulated advantages and leads to severe inequality. To overcome these limitations, we develop a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework in which a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies. Simulation results under four representative network topologies show that the learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels and average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared with the baselines. Furthermore, we interpret the learned policy and distill it into two simpler mechanisms: a resource-dependent mixture mechanism for regular networks and a degree-conditioned mixture mechanism for heterogeneous networks. These mechanisms reveal that effective allocation should adapt to both local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from reinforcement learning policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design allocation mechanisms in network common-pool resource games, focusing on cooperation and fairness, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To overcome limitations of equal and proportional allocation mechanisms in sustaining cooperation and reducing inequality in networked resource-sharing systems.
method: A graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework where a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without controlling individual strategies.
result: The learned planner sustains higher cooperation, higher average resources, and reduces inequality compared to baselines; the policy is distilled into simpler mechanisms adapted to network topology.
conclusion: Effective allocation should adapt to local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from RL policy search to mechanism design.

title: The Complexity Of Asynchronous HyperLTL
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperproperties express, e.g., information-flow properties of systems, which involves the simultaneous reasoning about multiple execution traces of a system. Consequently, HyperLTL, the most important specification logic for hyperproperties, extends LTL with quantification over traces. However, HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties. Recently, several logics for asynchronous hyperproperties have been proposed. Here, we focus on AHLTL, asynchronous HyperLTL, which extends HyperLTL with quantification over trajectories that control the relative speed at which time progresses on the quantified traces. Model-checking AHLTL is known to be undecidable while satisfiability is known to be [MATH]-hard, but the precise complexity of both problems is open. Here, we close these gaps and show that model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic while satisfiability is [MATH]-complete if the trajectory is existentially quantified and [MATH]-hard and in [MATH] if the trajectory is universally quantified.
tldr: This paper settles the complexity of model-checking and satisfiability for asynchronous HyperLTL, showing model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic and satisfiability is Σ1^1-complete or Π1^1-hard/Π1^1 depending on quantifier type.
motivation: HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties, but many information-flow properties require asynchronous reasoning. The precise complexity of AHLTL (asynchronous HyperLTL) was unknown, hindering its practical use.
method: The authors use reductions from second-order arithmetic and known hard problems to establish completeness results for model-checking and satisfiability of AHLTL.
result: Model-checking AHLTL is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic (highly undecidable). Satisfiability is Σ1^1-complete for existential trajectory quantification and Π1^1-hard and in Π1^1 for universal trajectory quantification.
conclusion: AHLTL is extremely expressive but computationally intractable, suggesting that practical verification of asynchronous hyperproperties may require restricted fragments or alternative logics.

title: Regret Minimization In Single-Dimensional Contract-Design With Binary Actions
authors: Riccardo Poiani, Martino Bernasconi, Andrea Celli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal-agent problems in which a principal commits to an outcome-dependent payment scheme (i.e., a contract) in order to induce an agent to take a costly action leading to a favorable outcome. We consider the online extension of the classical (one-shot) principal-agent problem, in which the principal repeatedly interacts with agents by proposing contracts over multiple rounds. The principal has no information about the agents and, crucially, does not observe their actions. As a result, the principal must learn an optimal contract using only the realized outcomes observed at each round. We focus on the setting with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, where the agent's private type represents their cost per unit-of-effort. For adversarial-type sequences, we provide tight [MATH] regret guarantees. Remarkably, this rate is completely independent of the number of outcomes [MATH]. The upper bound is based on two key components: 1) a reduction to a one-dimensional threshold optimization problem and 2) a non-uniform discretization to handle the non-Lipschitz nature of the problem. Moreover, in the case of a single (fixed) hidden type, we show that it is possible to improve the rates and provide a tight [MATH] regret bound. Our algorithm is based on an explore-then-commit strategy where we first approximately learn the hidden type via a stochastic binary search, and then we commit to a ``robustified'' near-optimal contract.
tldr: This paper studies online contract design with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, providing regret bounds for learning optimal contracts without observing agent actions.
motivation: To understand how a principal can learn an optimal contract over multiple rounds when agents' actions are unobservable and their types are unknown.
method: Reduces the problem to one-dimensional threshold optimization and uses non-uniform discretization to handle non-Lipschitzness; for fixed hidden type, uses explore-then-commit with stochastic binary search.
result: Tight Θ(T^{2/3}) regret for adversarial-type sequences, independent of number of outcomes; improved Θ(√T) regret for a single fixed hidden type.
conclusion: Provides fundamental regret bounds for online contract design, with implications for principal-agent problems in repeated settings.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization

tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and cell density control phase transitions in tissue organization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how mechanical properties like adhesion and jamming regulate tissue material state and developmental programs.
method: Combined in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.

title: Orbital Angular Momentum Multiplexing Diffractive Neural Networks For High-capacity Optical Inference
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents an orbital angular momentum multiplexing diffractive neural network for high-capacity optical inference, achieving 14-fold higher mode utilization and multitask recognition of 100 object categories.
motivation: To overcome the limited mode utilization in conventional orbital angular momentum multiplexing systems and enable high-capacity optical computing for multitask inference.
method: An end-to-end auto-optimization strategy is developed to design diffractive neural networks that exploit orbital angular momentum modes for multiplexing, replacing manual encoding.
result: The approach achieves 14-fold higher mode utilization compared to manual encoding and demonstrates multitask recognition of 100 object categories with an average accuracy of 72.7%.
conclusion: The work advances optical neural networks by leveraging orbital angular momentum multiplexing, potentially enabling high-capacity, low-power optical inference systems.

title: Crystalline Symmetry Breaking Enables Directional Light Emission In Quantum Dots
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports that crystalline symmetry breaking in quantum dots enhances light out-coupling efficiency, achieving high external quantum efficiencies in green QD-LEDs.
motivation: To improve the light extraction efficiency of quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs), which is limited by total internal reflection and waveguide modes.
method: The authors introduce crystalline symmetry breaking in zinc-blende quantum dots to modify the emission pattern and enhance out-coupling, and fabricate green CdZnSe- and InP-based QD-LEDs.
result: External quantum efficiencies of 34.3% for CdZnSe and 31.0% for InP-based QD-LEDs were achieved.
conclusion: This approach offers a new route to high-efficiency QD-LEDs without complex photonic structures, with potential for display and lighting applications.

title: An On-chip Programmable Valley Optoelectronic Nanocircuit

method: Integration of meta-waveguide photodetectors with transition metal dichalcogenides to create a light-programmable valley optoelectronic nanocircuit.
result: In situ generation, selective routing, and electrical readout of valley-dependent chiral photons were demonstrated.
conclusion: This work advances valleytronics by providing a programmable platform for on-chip valley optoelectronic circuits, with potential applications in quantum information processing and nanophotonics.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the evolution of atomic force microscopy from a surface imaging tool to a versatile nanoscience platform.

method: Commentary and historical review of technological advancements in AFM.
result: AFM has evolved beyond imaging to enable nanomechanical, electrical, and chemical measurements at the nanoscale.

title: Transparent Conducting Electrodes For Perovskite–silicon Tandem Solar Cells

method: The paper is a review that examines how optical, electrical and interfacial losses arise in tandem cells and outlines strategies to enable scalable, low-indium electrodes.

result: LegoNE discovered new equilibrium algorithms that outperform previous approaches in multi-player settings.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of LLMs for algorithm discovery in game theory, but its relevance to quantum information and thermodynamics is minimal.
